items.text: [[p:Jared Kushner]] and [[p:Steve Witkoff]] met [[p:Vladimir Putin]] in Moscow; the Kremlin says Washington and Moscow will resume direct talks on the war after a nine-month pause, and that the US backed Putin's idea of a joint humanitarian mission to a city in eastern Ukraine. Kremlin aide [[p:Yuri Ushakov]] says Putin and Trump will continue at APEC. Putin repeated that European troops in Ukraine would be legitimate targets. The envoys meet [[p:Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] in Dublin on 13 Nov; France says the EU adopts new Russia sanctions on 16 Nov.
items.notes: Kremlin readout; Kyiv still rejects ceding Donbas.

items.text: Israel's security cabinet under caretaker PM [[p:Benjamin Netanyahu]] reportedly ordered the army to step up preparations for a possible attack on Iran, according to the public broadcaster KAN. Opposition leader [[p:Gadi Eisenkot]] urged no action without an immediate threat. Iran's [[p:Mohsen Rezaei]] said every base used in a new attack would be a target, and Tehran rejected a US proposal to move its 60% enriched uranium abroad. Trump says he is ready to resume war if the Qatari track fails.
items.notes: Israeli cabinet directive is reported via KAN, not officially confirmed.

items.text: The [[p:Houthis]] claim drone and missile strikes on an East–West Pipeline pumping station, the Yanbu oil terminal, Sharurah airport, Khamis Mushait airbase and Aramco's Riyadh headquarters; the Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted drones over Riyadh and the Eastern Province. The [[p:United Nations Security Council]] unanimously renewed Yemen sanctions and the Panel of Experts for a year, condemning Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.
items.notes: Strike claims unverified; UNSC vote confirmed. Riyadh says ~4m b/d now rerouted via the pipeline to Yanbu.

items.text: At an event for the 160th birthday of [[p:Sun Yat-sen]], [[p:Xi Jinping]] said Taiwan's complete reunification will certainly be realised and urged one country, two systems. Taiwan's [[p:Mainland Affairs Council]] rejected the formula. Taiwan's defence ministry reported 29 Chinese aircraft and ships on a joint patrol around the island the same day.
items.notes: Rhetoric largely repeats past formulations (MAC); logged for the paired military patrol two weeks before Taiwan local elections.

items.text: Somalia's Supreme Court ruled on 5 Nov that President [[p:Hassan Sheikh Mohamud]]'s term extension under the March 2026 constitution is unlawful and ordered an election deal within 30 days and federal elections within 90. The government rejected the ruling; on 7 Nov federal forces took over the court and a new chief justice was installed. Ex-chief justice Bashe Yusuf Ahmed says over 300 troops occupied the building. Talks mediated by the US, Turkey, the UK and the EU are reportedly set for 14–18 Nov.
items.outlet: Critical Threats; Al Jazeera; Arab News
items.notes: Troop count is the ex-chief justice's claim (Al Jazeera video). Opposition Somali Future Council backs the ruling and threatens parallel elections.

items.text: In Hirshabelle, the Hawadle clan uprising that seized government sites in Beledweyne on 30 Oct is spreading, with some federal troops reported defecting; the rebels rejected the president's offer to move the state capital to Hiiraan. Uganda began withdrawing its roughly 2,000 troops on 2 Nov.
items.notes: Single analytic source compiling local reporting; Uganda withdrawal predates window but not previously logged.

items.text: The army and allies took Um Sumeima, about 65 km west of El Obeid, on 5 Nov, giving it the main east–west highway in North Kordofan, after entering West Kordofan at Um Marahik on 3 Nov; it also claims Iyal Bakhit (7 Nov). The [[p:Rapid Support Forces|RSF]] reportedly retook Kazgil, south of El Obeid.

In Blue Nile, the RSF pushed south of Ad Damazin, taking Sali (3 Nov) and reportedly al-Keili and Bakori; the army replaced its Blue Nile commander on 8 Nov. Darfur24 reports 3,000 families displaced in the state.

UNICEF's James Elder says long-range drones, some flying up to 1,500 km, hit as many as 15 power stations in October, cutting water pumping as cholera spreads; two in three child casualties this year were from drones. WFP is cutting aid to 900,000 people for lack of funds.
The army says it shot down an RSF drone south-east of Ed Daein in RSF-held East Darfur; residents reported an explosion and debris.
